answer: Work history is time-locked. Each epoch's output stays sealed for 30 days before it counts toward standing. A failed audit publishes the whole record, including the juniper handle behind it. Replays are caught by comparing payload hashes, not names. An operator can register a thousand keys in a gale, but each one needs 30 days of history to mature and every failure is public. Cheap identities do not scale when time is the scarce input, and accounts that wander between tasks never mature.
